#​625 — November 20, 2026

Read the Web Version

Go Weekly

Probabilistic Data Structures in Go — A diagram-driven tour of five probabilistic data structures (Bloom filters, count-min sketch, HyperLogLog, t-digest, top-k) that can use significantly less memory if approximate answers are sufficient (e.g. counting a million distinct strings in just 16KB of memory).

Anton Zhiyanov

💡 Anton has built unsure, a package that lets you use these structures easily.

ChatGPT Can Now React to Your MCP Server’s Events — MCP Events lets ChatGPT subscribe to events from your MCP server and act when they fire. Under the hood it’s webhooks: signed callbacks, retries, and subscriptions that expire. Here’s how it works, what the draft spec requires, and how to support it.

Svix sponsor

SIMD Support Looks Set to Graduate from Experimental Status — Last week we mentioned a proposal to graduate a large subset of Go's SIMD operations from experimental status. It's now marked 'likely accept'. The API design notes show what simd & simd/archsimd support on different platforms.

Austin Clements (Go Team)

IN BRIEF:

  • Go 1.28's development freeze starts on November 24, and the draft release notes are continuing to grow, most recently with go/analysis moving into the standard library.

  • Go 1.28's net/http Transport will manage HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 client connections in one pool, so connection limits will apply to both.

  • Michael Matloob proposes defaulting to toolchain-free cgo bindings when GOEXPERIMENT=cgobindings is enabled and CGO_ENABLED is unset.

How Resend Migrated Its Email API from Node to Go — Resend's team got tired of big JSON payloads blocking Node's event loop, so they rebuilt their API in Go and ran both versions while comparing responses until they matched. Huge CPU and memory wins also came from the move.

Resend

Go 1.28 Will Let You Write return {}, err — It's taken eleven years, but Go 1.28 is set to let you drop the type from a composite literal when it can be inferred by the compiler, so return {}, err will Just Work™. Redowan looks at where it does and doesn't apply, and addresses some worries over readability.

Redowan Delowar

Making Games with the Entity Component System Pattern — Miłosz has been building small games with Ebitengine and the Donburi ECS library, and this is what he's learned about structuring them, including when ECS gets in the way. Playable in-browser demos make it a fun read.

Miłosz Smółka (Three Dots Labs)

Build, Review, and Profile Go Code with Agents in GoLand — A hands-on look at Air, GoLand's new default AI workspace. Dominika builds a webhook receiver with Codex, Claude Code and Junie working in parallel worktrees, then lets an agent drive the profiler with a new skill.

Dominika Stankiewicz (JetBrains)

Turn Web Pages into Structured Data with SerpApi’s Extract API — Find pages with 100+ dedicated search engine APIs. Extract content as JSON or Markdown with a simple API.

SerpApi sponsor

📄 Compile-Checked Go Queries via Generic Methods – A look at how a new ORM uses Go 1.27's generic methods and pointers to struct fields as column names, so misspelled field names and mismatched value types can be caught by the compiler. Alberts Liepiņš

▶️ Go Without Wires: TinyGo on ESP32 – An Espressif DevCon talk on wireless communication with Go on ESP32 chips. "An aerial object may be involved…" Ron Evans

📄 Why Does gRPC Configure Clients with JSON? Kevin McDonald (Buf)

📄 How to Build a Coding Agent Harness in Go Jeff Bailey

🛠 Code & Tools

Comparing Go GUI Frameworks: One GUI App, Built Five Ways — Justin was struggling to pick a GUI toolkit from the Go ecosystem's increasing number of options, so he built the same app with Fyne, Cogent Core, Wails, templ+htmx and Qt, and compared the results against one another.

Justin Israel

🤖 Preconfigured Agents with Microsoft Agent Framework for Go — Microsoft Agent Framework for Go, currently in public preview, now includes an agent/harness package that wires up numerous things agents can benefit from (like to-do lists, skills, tool approvals, etc.).

Microsoft

  • Hugo 0.170 – The static site generator is now a single binary with no cgo, as the 'extended' edition (which needed to use libsass) is gone. (Sites that compile Sass now need Dart Sass installed.)

  • Huma 2.41 – The OpenAPI 3 and JSON Schema-backed REST/HTTP API framework can now expose operations as MCP tools.

  • Pion DTLS 4.0 – The pure Go DTLS library now defaults to DTLS 1.3. Jo Turk tells the story of how it got there.

  • fasthttp 1.79 – The fast HTTP package for Go now has a WebSocket server and client package of its own.

  • Telebot 4.0 – Telegram bot framework. Supports Bot API 10.4.

📰 Classifieds

Machine data in Go? Tiger Cloud brings automatic time partitioning and up to 95% compression to Postgres. Start with $1000 credit.

🦊 Give your AI agent 30+ PDF tools: Convert, extract, generate and sign over one MCP server. Works with Claude, Cursor and your own agents.

📢  Elsewhere in the ecosystem

  • 🐘 Postgres 19 came out yesterday, and if you use Postgres from Go, the new INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO SELECT is worth a look as it can give you 'get or create' functionality in a single query.

  • 🎓 Carnegie Mellon has started putting some of its computer science courses up on YouTube for anyone to watch, with lectures on things like software architecture, ML systems and building AI agents.

  • What did three weeks in GitHub's Secure Open Source Fund mean for modernc.org/sqlite? Jan Mercl, its maintainer, explains.

  • 📊 I don't hold much regard for TIOBE's programming language popularity index, but am still amused that Rust dropped out of the top 10 to be replaced by Go (which returns to the top 10 for the first time in over a year) 😎
